normalized_proposition: The Regulation establishes a Social Climate Fund for 2026–2032 to support Member State Plans' measures and investments addressing the social impacts of emissions-trading coverage of buildings and road transport.
Each Member State must prepare and submit a Plan with prescribed content (measures, investments, milestones, targets, consultation summary, control arrangements; template in Annex V).
Member States must consult listed stakeholder categories before submitting the Plan and include in the Plan a summary of the consultation and of how input is reflected.

The Commission assesses Plans on relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and coherence criteria (Art. 16(3)); the criteria are qualitative and no numeric threshold, weight or scoring rule for 'complies satisfactorily' is stated.

Payment is conditioned on satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones and targets, assessed by the Commission on a payment request; unmet milestones lead to suspension, proportional reduction and termination of agreements, with an opportunity for Member State observations.

Payment of financial allocations is also subject to availability of funding, equal treatment of Member States, pro-rata payment where assigned revenue is insufficient in a payment round, and allocation of unused appropriations after 31 December 2033 (Art. 20(1), (3), (9), (10)).

Additional statement-level evidence propositions in provisions not individually anchored in the other arm (e.g. Art. 14–15 allocation/contribution rules, Art. 22–23 coordination/communication, Annex II allocation table, Annex IV indicator list).
common_corpus_refs: Art. 14; Art. 15; Art. 22–23; Annexes II, IV

normalized_proposition: The Commission transmits Plans and decisions to the European Parliament and Council; Parliament committees may invite the Commission to discuss Plans, assessments, milestone status and payment/suspension/termination procedures; the Commission must take account of views expressed; the Commission provides interim and ex post evaluation reports to four Union bodies.

Member States must operate an internal control system (Annex III), accompany payment requests with a management declaration and audit summary, authorise Commission, OLAF, Court of Auditors and (where applicable) EPPO audit/control rights, and the Commission may reduce support and recover amounts in cases of fraud, corruption, conflict of interest or breach of obligations.

Member States may route support through public or private entities and must provide statutory and contractual safeguards ensuring the entire benefit is passed on to vulnerable households, micro-enterprises and transport users.
Member States report biennially on Plan implementation with common indicators; the Commission monitors using the same indicators.

Member State submits its Plan to the Commission; the Commission assesses it for compliance (may request observations/information within two months; Member State provides information; deadline extendable by agreement).
The Commission decides on the Plan by implementing act (allocation, measures, milestones, targets), may require additional internal-control measures, and a negatively assessed Plan is resubmitted.

Amendment of an approved Plan: the Member State submits an amended Plan when the Plan is no longer achievable; the Commission assesses it, adopts a decision by implementing act within three months, or rejects it after hearing the Member State; minor adjustments are notified.
The Commission supports Member States with technical guidance, examples of good practice and a common carbon-price value, and carries out joint communication activities with national authorities.
The Commission verifies, within its Plan assessment, that the Plan was developed in consultation with the listed stakeholders.

The Commission provides non-repayable support to Member States under direct management through an individual agreement; the Member State submits a reasoned payment request; the Commission assesses it and authorises disbursement.

On unmet milestones/targets the Commission suspends the proportional part of payment, reduces the allocation after nine months and terminates agreements after 15 months without tangible progress, in each case after the Member State may present observations.

Member States operate controls, designate implementing, signing and audit authorities (Annex III), accompany payment requests with a management declaration and audit summary, keep records and ensure access; recipients are bound to allow audit.

The Commission, OLAF, the Court of Auditors and (for participating Member States) the EPPO hold audit/control rights authorised through the agreements; the Commission may reduce support and recover amounts for specified breaches after hearing the Member State.

Member State–to–beneficiary pass-through: where support is channelled through public or private entities, the Member State must ensure by safeguards that the entire benefit reaches vulnerable households, micro-enterprises and transport users.
Member States report biennially to the Commission on Plan implementation using common indicators.

The Commission transmits Plans and decisions to the European Parliament and Council simultaneously; Parliament committees may invite the Commission to give information on the state of play of Plan assessment.
Competent Parliament committees may invite the Commission twice a year to the social climate dialogue; the Commission must take account of elements arising from views expressed and resolutions.
The Commission provides interim (two years after start of implementation) and independent ex post (by 31 Dec 2033) evaluation reports to the Parliament, Council, EESC and Committee of the Regions.

Qualification of the Commission's relation toward the competent Parliament committees (invitation, dialogue, duty to take account): whether it amounts to accountability, to answerability only with unstated sufficiency, or to information/dialogue only.

Transfers and entrustment: Member States may request transfer of shared-management resources to the Fund (implemented directly by the Commission), may request in the Plan transfer of up to 15% of the annual allocation to shared-management programmes, may entrust cohesion managing authorities; the Commission assesses requested transfers; Art. 28 inserts the receiving-side rule.
common_corpus_refs: Art. 11(1)–(4); Art. 16(2); Art. 28 (inserting Art. 26a of Reg. 2021/1060)

normalized_proposition: Plan formation and authorisation: Plan preparation, consultation, Commission assessment and decision (and, where included, amendment) form one arrangement organised around approval of nationally designed measures.
Consultation sits inside (is nested in) the Plan-formation arrangement as a participation step followed by Commission verification.
Direct-managed, performance-conditioned financing: agreement, payment request, assessment, disbursement decision and enforcement branches (suspension, reduction, termination) form one arrangement.

Financial control: the national internal-control duties and Union audit/access/recovery relations form an arrangement; the question is whether it is the same arrangement as monitoring/evaluation and parliamentary information relations.
Monitoring, reporting and evaluation relations (Art. 24, 27) and their membership relative to the payment and control arrangements.
common_corpus_refs: Art. 24; Art. 27; Art. 6(1)(m); Art. 17(2)(d)–(e); Annex IV

normalized_proposition: Parliamentary information and dialogue relations (Art. 25–26) and their membership relative to the control arrangement.
Transfers between the Fund and shared-management programmes (request, Commission assessment, direct or programme-level implementation) form an arrangement.
Overlap and nesting among arrangements: consultation nested in plan formation; payment/enforcement and control share relations; monitoring and parliamentary dialogue share relations.

The Regulation constitutes a formal governance architecture organised around Plan approval, Commission decision and performance-conditioned payment, with national implementation under financial control (bounded to the Regulation; formal design only).

Number and boundary of architectures: one architecture covering the whole Fund design (including monitoring/evaluation and parliamentary information), versus one architecture covering plan–payment–control–transfer arrangements plus a separate partially integrated monitoring candidate and an indeterminate parliamentary-dialogue candidate, with merger into one whole-instrument architecture treated as not warranted.

Whether the monitoring, reporting and evaluation relations (Art. 24, 27) belong inside the same architecture as the plan–payment–control relations, given that the reports are not stated to feed the payment assessment but share the Annex IV indicator interface with the Plan and the Commission decision.
Whether the Commission–Parliament information and dialogue relations form part of the architecture as an accountability dimension, or leave the accountability claim indeterminate.
Whether the transfer relations (Art. 11, 16(2), 28) are inside the Fund architecture, or the Art. 28 interface remains outside it.

Centralisation/vertical distribution: decision competence over Plans and payments rests with the Commission, while implementation and control functions are distributed across Union, national and sub-national levels; no single 'centralised' label for the whole.
common_corpus_refs: Art. 12; Art. 16–17; Art. 20; Art. 21; Annex III

normalized_proposition: Accountability as an architectural property: one combined accountability arrangement (information, assessment and consequences) versus differentiated values by forum — Member State to Commission (sufficient within the corpus), information-only relations to Union institutions, and answerability with indeterminate sufficiency toward Parliament committees — with no composite.

Discretion distribution: Member States hold Plan-content discretion; the Commission holds bounded evaluative discretion in assessing criteria and 'satisfactory' achievement; sanctions follow mandatory wording once findings are made.

Directness/intermediation: the Commission–Member State financing leg is direct; Member States are the intermediary toward final recipients; optional channelling through public/private entities does not make the architecture intermediary-centred.

Absence-dependent negative attributes: no multiple partly autonomous decision centres for Fund allocation, no self-regulatory capacity, no intermediary-centred architecture; the Commission as sole holder of decision competence over Plans and payments within the corpus, given that the adoption procedure of implementing acts is not stated in the Regulation.
Whether the Commission's Plan decision and payment decision are a necessary, non-substitutable stage for every payment of Fund resources.

Functional allocation, sequence and depth: functions are allocated across implementation, verification/assurance, enforcement and information; the funding sequence runs from agreement to payment with enforcement branches.
The rule-making position (the legislator) is not a party to any relation of the Regulation; no path depth from it is attributed.
common_corpus_refs: Art. 25–27 (Parliament and Council appear only as recipients/forum)

normalized_proposition: The Fund design is characterised as 'control-intensive' at the whole-architecture level on the basis of the number and layering of ex ante, reporting, audit, access, recovery and payment-consequence provisions.
common_corpus_refs: Art. 5–6; Art. 16–17; Art. 20–21; Art. 24–27; Annex III

normalized_proposition: The claims concern legal assignments, powers and procedures only; implementation, exercise, effectiveness and actual practice are not asserted.

External legal dependencies as sensitivity of conclusions: payment, commitment, direct-management, transfer, reporting-vehicle, control-rights and discharge propositions rest partly on legal sources outside the Regulation (Financial Regulation, Directive 2003/87/EC, Regulation 2021/1060, Regulation 2018/1999, TFEU Art. 319); the claims should or should not be limited to the Regulation's text.

Rival groupings and boundary sensitivities for the architecture: plan and payment arrangements as two architectures joined only at the Art. 17 decision; national internal control as a separate architecture; merger of all candidates into one whole-instrument architecture.

Stopping level: both arms stop at the architectural level (below regime level); for the parliamentary-dialogue and monitoring parts RGAM stops below the architectural level (indeterminate/partial) while V8 includes them in the architecture.

Confidence in the architecture claim is qualified: medium-high with analytical characterisations flagged (V8); outcome scoped to the corpus with unvalidated coupling thresholds and provisional status (RGAM).
Higher-order constructs (regime membership; strategies and logics of governance) beyond the architecture.
Practical range of discretion and effectiveness of consultation, controls and reporting are uncertain and not asserted.
Counterparty/direction uncertainty where the text states no recipient or obligor (e.g. request under Art. 14(2), observations under Art. 20(4), information duties in Art. 23(2), 24(3), 28).
